Implement "Shared-hosting subdomain SSL" for the Nxeon platform. Work EXCLUSIVELY in the git worktree at /opt/nxeon-wt-subdomain-ssl (branch feature/hosting-subdomain-ssl). Do not touch /opt/nxeon or other worktrees. node_modules is symlinked there.

GOAL (board card): shared-hosting accounts can add subdomains (the feature exists) but those subdomains need working SSL. Ensure subdomain vhosts get valid HTTPS certs — either via per-name certbot issuance covering the subdomain, or a wildcard cert for the account's primary domain. Read the current implementation FIRST and extend it correctly.

RULES: Do NOT run any build/prisma command — write code only. Study the existing hosting SSL machinery before changing anything:
- worker/hosting.ts (certbot/SSL issuance, vhost generation, the post-DNS SSL sweep, SNI handling) — there is already a webroot certbot flow with `--allow-subset-of-names` and a serving verifier.
- lib/actions-hosting.ts (subdomain add/list actions) and the DatabasesPanel/Domains hosting UI.
- How addon domains vs subdomains are modeled (grep the schema + isHostnameClaimed).

BUILD: make subdomains get HTTPS. The cleanest approach is usually: when a subdomain is added (and its DNS resolves to the node), include it in the account's certbot certificate (expand the existing webroot issuance to cover primary + www + each active subdomain, reusing --allow-subset-of-names so partial DNS doesn't abort), regenerate the vhost to serve 443 for it, and let the existing SSL sweep pick it up. Follow the EXISTING patterns (idempotent, guarded, sshd -t style safety, the settle/verify loop). Do not weaken the cross-tenant isolation fixes (disable_symlinks, open_basedir, hostname-claim guard).

Keep it tight and reuse the audited flow. DELIVER end-to-end (worker + any action/UI touch), then in the worktree: `git add -A && git commit -m "feat: HTTPS for shared-hosting subdomains (certbot SAN expansion + vhost 443)"` (trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>), then `git push -u origin feature/hosting-subdomain-ssl`. REPORT (factual): files changed, the exact issuance approach (SAN expansion vs wildcard) and why, how it stays idempotent, and any DNS/wildcard prerequisite. Don't claim tested.

105	async function run(conn: Client, label: string, cmd: string): Promise<void> {
106	  const r = await exec(conn, cmd, STEP_TIMEOUT_MS);
107	  if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(`${label} failed: ${r.out.slice(0, 300)}`);
108	}
109	
110	/**
111	 * The name-based nginx vhost for one account. It ALWAYS emits a `listen 443 ssl`
112	 * server block so nginx answers HTTPS from the moment the account exists —
113	 * `ssl.certDir` is the real Let's Encrypt live dir when `ssl.real` is true, else
114	 * the per-account SELF-SIGNED fallback generated at provision time. That is the
115	 * whole "clean setup always" guarantee: HTTPS shows a cert WARNING, never
116	 * ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED. The HTTP→HTTPS redirect fires ONLY once a real cert
117	 * exists; a self-signed site still serves its body over both 80 and 443 (so it
118	 * can't 301-loop a visitor into an untrusted-cert dead end). Shared IP; routed
119	 * purely by server_name; PHP proxied to THIS account's socket only, root jailed to
120	 * its webroot. Pure string — no interpolation reaches a shell here.
121	 */
122	function renderHostingVhost(username: string, domain: string, webroot: string, sock: string, ssl: { certDir: string; real: boolean }): string {
123	  const phpLoc = [
124	    `    location ~ \\.php$ {`,
125	    `        include fastcgi_params;`,
126	    `        fastcgi_pass unix:${sock};`,
127	    `        fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $document_root$fastcgi_script_name;`,
128	    `    }`,
129	  ].join("\n");
130	  const body = [
131	    `    root ${webroot};`,
132	    // Refuse to follow a symlink whose target isn't owned by the same user as the
133	    // link — blocks a tenant symlinking to a victim's wp-config.php that nginx
134	    // (www-data) would otherwise happily serve (cross-tenant read, audit CRITICAL-1).
135	    `    disable_symlinks if_not_owner;`,
136	    `    index index.php index.html;`,
137	    `    location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$query_string; }`,
138	    phpLoc,
139	    `    location ~ /\\. { deny all; }`,
140	  ].join("\n");
141	  const http = [
142	    `server {`,
143	    `    listen 80;`,
144	    `    listen [::]:80;`,
145	    `    server_name ${domain} www.${domain};`,
146	    `    location ^~ /.well-known/acme-challenge/ { root /var/www/html; }`,
147	    // Redirect to HTTPS only with a REAL cert; a self-signed site serves over 80 too.
148	    ssl.real ? `    location / { return 301 https://$host$request_uri; }` : body,
149	    `}`,
150	  ].join("\n");
151	  const https = [
152	    `server {`,
153	    `    listen 443 ssl;`,
154	    `    listen [::]:443 ssl;`,
155	    `    server_name ${domain} www.${domain};`,
156	    `    ssl_certificate ${ssl.certDir}/fullchain.pem;`,
157	    `    ssl_certificate_key ${ssl.certDir}/privkey.pem;`,
158	    `    ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;`,
159	    body,
160	    `}`,
161	  ].join("\n");
162	  return `${http}\n${https}\n`;
163	}
164	
165	/** Write a vhost file + enable it, tested before reload. */
166	async function installVhost(conn: Client, username: string, conf: string): Promise<void> {
167	  const path = `/etc/nginx/sites-available/hosting-${username}.conf`;
168	  await run(conn, "write vhost", `cat > ${path} <<'VH'\n${conf}VH\nln -sfn ${path} /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/hosting-${username}.conf`);
169	  await run(conn, "test + reload nginx", `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`);
170	}

173	 * A single extra site (subdomain / addon domain): its own docroot + PHP socket,
174	 * one `server_name`. Same shape as renderHostingVhost but keyed on an explicit
175	 * server_name string so it can serve a subdomain OR an addon domain. Pure — no
176	 * interpolation reaches a shell here (the caller validated every part).
177	 */
178	function renderSiteVhost(serverName: string, docroot: string, sock: string, sslLiveDir: string | null): string {
179	  const phpLoc = [
180	    `    location ~ \\.php$ {`,
181	    `        include fastcgi_params;`,
182	    `        fastcgi_pass unix:${sock};`,
183	    `        fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $document_root$fastcgi_script_name;`,
184	    `    }`,
185	  ].join("\n");
186	  const body = [
187	    `    root ${docroot};`,
188	    // Refuse a symlink whose target isn't owned by the link's owner — a tenant
189	    // can't symlink a neighbour's file into a served path (audit CRITICAL-1).
190	    `    disable_symlinks if_not_owner;`,
191	    `    index index.php index.html;`,
192	    `    location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$query_string; }`,
193	    phpLoc,
194	    `    location ~ /\\. { deny all; }`,
195	  ].join("\n");
196	  const http = [
197	    `server {`,
198	    `    listen 80;`,
199	    `    listen [::]:80;`,
200	    `    server_name ${serverName};`,
201	    `    location ^~ /.well-known/acme-challenge/ { root /var/www/html; }`,
202	    sslLiveDir ? `    location / { return 301 https://$host$request_uri; }` : body,
203	    `}`,
204	  ].join("\n");
205	  if (!sslLiveDir) return http + "\n";
206	  const https = [
207	    `server {`,
208	    `    listen 443 ssl;`,
209	    `    listen [::]:443 ssl;`,
210	    `    server_name ${serverName};`,
211	    `    ssl_certificate ${sslLiveDir}/fullchain.pem;`,
212	    `    ssl_certificate_key ${sslLiveDir}/privkey.pem;`,
213	    `    ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;`,
214	    body,
215	    `}`,
216	  ].join("\n");
217	  return `${http}\n${https}\n`;
218	}

220	/** Write + enable a vhost under an arbitrary key (hosting-<key>.conf), tested
221	 *  before reload. Used for subdomain / addon-domain sites (key = <user>-<label>
222	 *  or <user>-<domain>); the account's own primary vhost keeps its <user> filename. */
223	async function installNamedVhost(conn: Client, key: string, conf: string): Promise<void> {
224	  const path = `/etc/nginx/sites-available/hosting-${key}.conf`;
225	  await run(conn, "write site vhost", `cat > ${path} <<'VH'\n${conf}VH\nln -sfn ${path} /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/hosting-${key}.conf`);
226	  await run(conn, "test + reload nginx", `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`);
227	}
228	
229	/** Remove a named site vhost (enabled + available), tested before reload. */
230	async function removeNamedVhost(conn: Client, key: string): Promise<void> {
231	  await run(conn, "remove site vhost", `rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/hosting-${key}.conf /etc/nginx/sites-available/hosting-${key}.conf; nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx || true`);
232	}

234	/** Write + (re)load an account's FPM pool for a given PHP version. The pool
235	 *  contents (the PHP isolation boundary) come from the tested pure generator in
236	 *  lib/hosting.ts — socket path is unchanged across versions so the vhost never
237	 *  needs editing when PHP is switched. */
238	async function writeFpmPool(conn: Client, u: string, home: string, webroot: string, php: string): Promise<void> {
239	  if (!/^\d\.\d$/.test(php)) throw new Error(`refusing unsafe php version ${php}`);
240	  await run(conn, "php-fpm pool", `cat > /etc/php/${php}/fpm/pool.d/${u}.conf <<'POOL'\n${fpmPoolConfig(u, home, webroot)}\nPOOL\nsystemctl reload php${php}-fpm 2>/dev/null || systemctl restart php${php}-fpm`);
241	}
242	
243	/**
244	 * The isolation shell for one account (HTTP-only vhost; SSL added later by the
245	 * sweep once DNS points at us). Every interpolated value has already cleared a
246	 * validator, so nothing here can be a shell metacharacter.
247	 */
248	async function applyIsolation(
249	  conn: Client,
250	  a: { username: string; primaryDomain: string; diskQuotaMB: number; sftpPassword: string },
251	  php: string,
252	): Promise<void> {
253	  const u = a.username;
254	  const d = a.primaryDomain;
255	  if (!isValidUnixUsername(u)) throw new Error(`refusing unsafe username ${u}`);
256	  if (!isValidHostingDomain(d)) throw new Error(`refusing unsafe domain ${d}`);
257	  if (!/^\d\.\d$/.test(php)) throw new Error(`refusing unsafe php version ${php}`);
258	  const { home, webroot } = accountPaths(u);
259	  const quotaGB = Math.max(1, Math.round(a.diskQuotaMB / 1024));
260	  const hardBlocks = diskQuotaBlocks(quotaGB);
261	  const softBlocks = Math.floor(hardBlocks * 0.95);
262	  const inodes = diskQuotaInodes(quotaGB);
263	  const sock = `/run/php/${u}.sock`;
264	
265	  // 1. Jailed user. Home is ROOT-owned (a chroot requirement); the user owns only
266	  //    public_html + tmp under it. nologin shell — SFTP-only via the chroot below.
267	  //

Done. Committed and pushed.

## Summary

Shared-hosting subdomains now get real HTTPS. Worked exclusively in `/opt/nxeon-wt-subdomain-ssl` on branch `feature/hosting-subdomain-ssl` (pushed).

### Files changed
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-subdomain-ssl/worker/hosting.ts` — added a subdomain SSL pass inside the existing `hostingSslSweep()` (after the primary + addon loops); updated the stale "left for a wildcard-cert follow-up" comment.
- `/opt/nxeon-wt-subdomain-ssl/components/customer/hosting/SubdomainsPanel.tsx` — HTTPS badge + `https://` link when `sslActive`, poll while an ACTIVE subdomain awaits its cert, corrected the help text (was "HTTPS for subdomains is a follow-up — they serve over HTTP until then").

### Issuance approach: SAN expansion, not wildcard
Each active subdomain is folded into its **account's existing Let's Encrypt lineage** as an additional SAN via the same HTTP-01 webroot flow the primary/addon certs already use:
`certbot certonly --webroot -w /var/www/html --cert-name <primary> -d <primary> -d www.<primary> -d <each sub>.<primary> --expand --allow-subset-of-names --non-interactive --agree-tos --register-unsafely-without-email --keep-until-expiring`

Then the subdomain vhost is reinstalled via the existing `renderSiteVhost(fqdn, docroot, sock, liveDir)` to serve `listen 443 ssl` off the account's live cert dir (`/etc/letsencrypt/live/<primary>`), and `sslActive` is flipped. SNI on the shared IP routes by `server_name`.

**Why SAN, not wildcard:** a wildcard requires DNS-01, which needs a DNS-provider API the platform doesn't hold (customers self-manage their own DNS). HTTP-01 SAN expansion works off the pointed A record — the exact mechanism every other cert here already relies on, and the subdomain's HTTP vhost already proxies `/.well-known/acme-challenge` to `/var/www/html`, so the challenge serves with no new plumbing.

### Idempotency / safety
- Only subdomains that currently resolve to the node IP (`domainPointsAt`) are folded in, so certbot never churns on an unvalidatable name; `--keep-until-expiring` makes an unchanged reissue a no-op; `--expand` only reissues when the SAN set actually grows.
- `--cert-name <primary>` pins the lineage so the live-dir path never changes (no `-0001` dirs); `--cert-name` matches the primary sweep's default lineage name (first `-d` = primary), so it expands the same cert rather than forking a new one.
- Already-secured subs are kept in the `-d` set (never dropped) and skipped for vhost reinstall — no churn on live subdomains; `--allow-subset-of-names` tolerates any name whose DNS lags.
- One reissue per account per sweep (dedup `Set`), guarded by `isValidUnixUsername`/`isValidSubdomainLabel`/`isValidHostingDomain`; before flipping `sslActive` it verifies via `openssl x509 ... grep -qiF 'DNS:<fqdn>'` that the cert genuinely covers the name.
- Cross-tenant isolation untouched: reuses `renderSiteVhost` verbatim (keeps `disable_symlinks if_not_owner`), the hostname-claim guard in `createSubdomain`, and the sshd/`nginx -t`-guarded install helpers. The account cert must already exist (primary sweep issues it first) or the sub is retried next tick.

### DNS prerequisite
A subdomain gets HTTPS only once an A record (or `*.<primary>` wildcard) for `<label>.<primary>` points at the node's shared IP — required for the HTTP-01 challenge. Until then it keeps serving over HTTP (self-signed fallback still prevents ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED on 443 at the account level). The sweep is inert unless `ENABLE_SHARED_HOSTING` and not in SANDBOX, consistent with every other node path.
